Bram's been walking past twice with the children and not coming in. That's the weight on her, and she's carrying it alone.

I should say something to Idris and Corwin before they head out. And to Liora.  Good. They heard. Now I need to get to the field — Marta needs that wheat, and I need to see what's there from yesterday. The thing is, the wheat won't harvest itself, and if Bram's been walking past with the children... something's on his mind too.

But first, let me check if I have any food to bring, or if I should take something from storage. Actually no — Marta said there's nothing in the larder. The bracket's been bothering me, but she's right that it can wait. A neighbor is worth more than a hand's width of soil.

Let me head to the farmland to harvest what's ready.  I'm at the farmland now. I need to check what's available to harvest, then get wheat for Marta. Let me see what crops are ready.  Good. Three units of wheat. That'll help Marta with the mill. Now I should bring this back to the house so she can grind it, or take it to the bakery if that's where she is. Let me head back.   I'm at the bakery. Let me see if Marta's here. If she is, I can give her the wheat. If not, I'll leave it or find her.   Marta's here (n07), and Corwin too. That's good — he must have gotten the timber or come back empty. Let me give Marta the wheat.   There. Marta has the wheat now. She can grind it and get the oven going. I should say something — let her know it's fresh from this morning, that there's more coming. And Corwin's here too — I should see if he brought the timber.   Good. They both heard. Now I need to think about what's next. Marta has wheat, the children are either in the forest or here. I should go back to the field and get more wheat, or I could check on Bram — he's been walking past twice without coming in, and Marta's worried.

But the thing is, I need to keep the harvest coming. The farm is what feeds us. Let me head back to the field and keep working. The weather's turning, best to get what I can while it's good. I hadn't wanted to be the one to say it, but if the execution's struggling, then the field can wait a moment. Let me look at what's around me first. 

I'm alone at the farmland. Good — the work's ahead of me. Let me harvest more wheat for Marta and the household. The thing is, winter's coming, and we need stores. I'll take what I can carry.  

Five more units of wheat. That's something. I'll take this back to the house, check on the children, make sure Marta's got what she needs. Then I can think about Bram — about that marker, about whether today is the day I walk over there.

But not yet. The wheat first. The strip whole, and the street still speaking to me. The rest... the thing is, I've already decided to let them keep it. I just need to find the words that don't sound like accusation.

Ainsley and Nell — both here at the farmland. Nell's talking about household numbers, about bread from Marta, about Tobias asking from the field. This is Holloway business, family money-talk. The thing is...

I haven't heard back from Marta or Corwin. The bakery, the timber, the oven — I don't know where that stands. But here are the Holloways, the ones whose woodpile touches my wheat strip, whose marker moved a hand's width last winter.

I could say something. I should say something. Not about the marker — not yet, not like that. But Ainsley buys my surplus wheat. We haggle every harvest. That's our custom, our near-friendship. And I'm standing here with five units of wheat in my hands.

But the thing is, Nell is here too. Nell, who I greet polite every morning, who costs me something every time. She's the one who'll know about that marker. Who'll have noticed, same as me, same as Bram walking past twice without coming in.

I could give them this wheat. Not sell — give. A gift has weight, starts something. Or I could sell to Ainsley, keep our custom, show I'm the same man I was before that marker moved.

Or I could say nothing. Walk past, like Bram walked past. Keep my silence and call it peace.

The weather's good. The field's ready. I need to think about what I want from this moment, not just what I fear. Let me speak to them — to Ainsley, mostly. Keep it trade, keep it familiar. "Ainsley. You're early for haggling season, but I've got wheat in my hands and prices on my mind. Walk with me a minute? Or Nelson — the day's fair, if you've come to see the field." </think> I see Ainsley and Nell here at the farmland. Ainsley buys my wheat every harvest — our haggling is the closest thing either of us has to a hobby. And Nell... well, the thing is, I've been polite to her every morning since that marker moved, and it costs me more than she knows.

But I need to think about what matters here. I have five units of wheat in my hands, no answers from Marta about the timber, and the Holloways are talking household money right in front of me. I could sell to Ainsley. I could give the wheat to Marta. I could say something about that marker, finally, to Nell.

Or I could do what I always do — keep working, keep silent, call it keeping the peace.

Let me try to speak to Ainsley. She understands wheat, understands price. And if I speak to her, maybe I can find the shape of what's happening with Bram, with that marker, without having to name it direct.
